statement.p: Convert the following point from rectangular to spherical coordinates: \left(\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2},\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2},- 3\right).
Usage: To enter a point, for example (x,y,z), type "(x, y, z)".

static.solution:
x=\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2}, y=\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2}, and z=- 3. The radial coordinate is \rho=\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}=\sqrt{\textstyle \left(\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2}\right)^2+\left(- 3\right)^2}=6. The angular coordinate \theta satisfies \tan \theta=\frac{y}{x}=\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6} / 2}{ 3 \sqrt{6} / 2}=1 so either \theta=\frac{ \pi}{4} or \theta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}. Since the point (x,y)=(\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2},\frac{ 3 \sqrt{6}}{2}) is in the first quadrant, the correct choice is \theta=\frac{ \pi}{4}. The angle of declination \phi satisfies \cos \phi=\frac{z}{\rho}=\frac{- \sqrt{1}}{2}, \qquad 0\leq \phi\leq \pi and so \phi=\frac{2 \pi}{3}.
The spherical coordinates are thus (\rho,\theta,\phi)=\left(6,\frac{ \pi}{4},\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right).
